140353.ques: What was the inspiration behind "i'm going off the map"?
140353.answ: writing songs is just what i do. according to my notes here, i came up with the first few bars and title on october 19, 2018. Which seems to be also the same day that i came up with starting ideas for 12 others, including "long long journey" and "just did a bad thing". The inspiration for this writing session of course would be that i was on a 2-week song production schedule and i'd just finished the previous song so it's time to do the next one. And typically that process starts by coming up with a whole bunch of new things, then doing a selection process which includes potentially any of those PLUS any of the ones before, from any level of writing completion. looks like that time around 'long journey' was the one that got selected, but it's good to see that the system works, seeing that the other ones seem to get selected in due time

140490.ques: there's a problem with me when i try to write music - i always go back to the same chord (or progression) i liked (and/or used) previously. and it's just like "wow we are back here again" and i'm just mad at myself (mostly annoying though). i don't know how to deal with this, my every improv session goes into some chord progression or melody in D (even when I am specifically trying to avoid D cuz im annoyed) and it feels like I can't escape that. any advice?
140490.answ: sure. what you're trying to escape now is not the key of D, it's not even any chord in particular. what you are trying to escape is THINKING about the chords. or just 'thinking' about what youre trying to do. if you think, it's all over. of course once you get to this ugly mindset, it can be a spiral because you dont know how to fix it. and in fact there is no way to fix it. except that it truly wants to fix itself. it's just waiting until you finally forget about trying to think about how to fix it. i'm sure i've made it out to sound like some mythical deity is in charge of your songwriting. but if you ask pretty much any songwriter who's ever written things, i can almost guarantee they would say that's exactly how it is

140557.answ: the first section is not very forthcoming about what key it's in, you might call it D something, maybe even G, who knows. by the time you hit 'remember where', that is very plainly in Eb. then for "down on the land", it sort of tricks you in that moment to think we might be in Eb minor but by the next bar we find out it's actually Bb minor. soon enough, at 'hope to understand' it is more like Db major which is really the same key anyway, then 'just about an hour ago' sits on an Ebsus2 chord not really having decided whether that's the 4 of Bb or something else, but it ends up on Gb which is the 4 of Db and we're still in Db for 'hour ago hour ago', all the way up to 'cling to you', then for 'sing to you' it swaps up to act like it's getting ready to land in E, but then as a surprise it lands in Ab instead for 'sing to me'. and we stay there for that whole section. then on 'heat it up' it jumps to some kind of D something, borrowing freely from D minor and D major, then lands decisively on a warm D major for "on the map" and stays in D for a long time. then as we get to 'hypnotizing me', it starts hovering on what still feels like a 5 chord in the key of D, for the whole 'mesmerize/tree' section, but then when we land on the riff, suddenly the A chord now sounds like the root so now we're in A something. A7 sort of thing, borrowing from minor and major as needed

141351.ques: I find it interesting that "i get turned on by the news" was written to mean "it is normal to get freaked out by the news because that's literally its job", I had always interpreted it as enjoying the news such that the person watching is complacent in whatever the news is talking about
141351.answ: keep in mind, the previous line was "turn on the news", so the fact that i use the phrase "turned on" was a bit of wordplay to match the previous line (it is a song after all). but indeed it is referring to the news's intended role of getting our attention by agitating us. if you watch the video for the song it may be a little more clear: there are flames on the screen. further playing into the trope that the news always tries their very best to find flames to show you, if they can. ah, now i remember, the next line also continues to explain this "the news gets more views whenever there's cool news", 'cool' in this case being a bit of a euphamism for..... attention getting, horrifying, etc

141513.ques: Bill, I really appreciate your extremely anti-AI sentiments which are strongly hinted at in your responses, not that I am surprised that an artist like yourself has such feelings about the tech being applied to art. In one question recently, you seemed to imply "off the map" was through composed because that seems less likely to be ai generated. Do you actually feel like you need to make some extra effort to prove your work is genuine? I hope you don't but i also understand and empathize with an incapability to not think about AI constantly these days. Here's to hoping it takes up less headspace in yours than mine (I work in tech). Thanks for all the brilliant work you've produced over the years. Your work has always been inspiring and incredibly moving.
141513.answ: "off the map" was already fully written in 2023, so i can't say that that's specifically the reason that it is the way it is. but it's always nice to try to step back and realize "slop" is not new. the mission of creativity is always to find new ways to prove we're alive. slop used to be made by hardworking uncreative people, now thankfully we can all more fully devote to genuine creativity. "verse chorus" is fine and great, and i have many songs written that use that. but i've always taken every opportunity to take the creative approach. for example, starting about 25 years ago we all started to notice it may be commonplace to actually copy the recording of the first chorus vocals to the second chorus. I mean, that's just a perfectly wasted opportunity. even if you only just change 1 word, change 1 little thing, that gives the audience a sign at least that you're there! that you haven't left the building and left the song on auto-play. so this is not really a new concept. so just as almost like a religion, i never copy vocals from 1 section to another, or even any instrumental parts. Like a mother to a child, i want to be there for you. you need to know i'm there. because, when i am on the listening side of things, when i'm the listener and you're the artist, i need to know you're there. that's what it all comes down to, at any point in our technological history. that's the core issue the audience needs to know: "are you really there?" and as artists, it's our job to prove we're really there. and as time goes by and the technology does this or that, the methods for proving you're really there will always have to change. that's what makes it so much fun. as everything changes, the core issue, and in fact the ONLY issue that ever remains constant is, "are you really there?" by the way, there's also no reason you cant use ai in all kinds of ways and still prove youre there. but it's too soon to see exactly how that plays out, and the audience needs time to get used to sorting it all out and knowing the difference. plus, as usual i tend not to get into big new technologies until maybe 10 years after the fact. so we'll see. but the miracle of all this, as always, is that it further clarifies our understanding of just what means something to us and what does not

141793.ques: you say you get ideas for your songs at unexpected moments. in that case, how do you retain them in your mind for long enough such that you can later write them down or record them to get back to them later? a lot of really cool songs i've invented have never come to be because I'm unable to remember them for long enough before I can play them, and it's very frustrating
141793.answ: if you really wanna catch it, you gotta catch it right when you get it. there's plenty of devices that can record your voice, most commonly a phone or something. if you cant speak into your phone, there are ways of writing it on paper if you have paper (notation systems, numbering systems, etc), but more likely you may only have access to text, such as on a touch screen on your phone, which is much less ideal, but if you can fight against the autocorrect you can write down some descriptions, melody rhythm and chord indications, and describe as specifically as you can what you're hearing. Now, .... if you don't have any way to accurately describe music to yourself, describe rhythms, describe melodies, etc, then that's something you'll need to develop. you can borrow from the notation systems that are widely in use, or you can make your own system that caters best to your needs. but one way or another you're going to need a way to communicate with yourself. for example, a carpenter probably has names for their tools, even if they made up their own names

141890.ques: so i just learned that you used a random number generator to decide which song to work on next (like and the day goes on), so does that mean that your recent (post 2020) songs also pull from that same set of old songs? or is it a mix of old and new? do you make an effort to pick the "best" songs?
141890.answ: trying to pick 'the best' usually means playing it way too safe. what you can do, however, is narrow it down to 5 or 10 that are very exciting, then secretly try to beef up each one of them in competition with the others. in other words, go around to each one and say, what would i need to do to this one to make it suddenly crush all the others. and you go around and keep doing that and strenghening all of them and making them fight with each other, until you essentially feel scared NOT to pick every single one of them. then you know you can be safe doing a random, and be assured that the selection is legitimate. Because, once you start production, you can and will begin to feel terrible from time to time, and if there is ANY doubt in the selection, you will fall apart and try to blame the selection. so that is how we ensure confidence in the selection. and so i am collecting from the entire list of everything i have, but i narrow it down to ones that seem the most exciting at that time. then i make them fight with each other, then i end up with 5 or 10 that i absolutely cant imagine NOT picking, then random from those. it's always interesting to look back and see what the other finalists were. for example, when 'soft clothing' got picked, with a different flip of the dice would one of 3 other songs been recorded instead, one of them is actually the one i'm doing now. and all 4 had probably been in the finals before. Sometimes one gets knocked out for awhile, for silly reasons like it collides with another one. for example, the one i'm working on now actually fell out of favor for a while after 'money', and previously also after 'first day of school think i might quit', due to certain surface-level similarities, so you want to let a bit more time pass before appearing to do two songs that maybe reference the same thing somewhere in them, or maybe have certain similar musical attributes such as tempo or time feel. for example there's another one that i really wanted to pick this time, but it has one tiny moment that is kind of a little bit similar to a moment in 'off the map'. so that one will be delayed for a little while but will probably come up again after a few more go by. the one i'm doing now has been around since 2018 (at least the first line was), and another one of the finalists this time was one with about a minute written in 2011 and about 30 more seconds written in 2025, which i expect will be pretty persistent and be selected soon. along with many, many others

141953.ques: do you have any tips for a speaking presentation i have to do in 8 days in front of my whole school that im woefully unprepared for pls help
141953.answ: the only way to get good at this is to do many many presentations. it doesnt really matter what you do on stage, you just have to spend enough time there to get used the crazy feeling so it doesnt distract you anymore. on the first time you will probably have no hope of feeling normal. after about 20 times, then you will begin to feel like yourself again. so basically what you wanna do is look at your schedule and see how many additional presentations can you schedule for yourself, in the next 8 days, before doing the other one. the other rule is, never think about what you think it would be like to be on stage before you've been there. you'll never be able to imagine what it's like, and you'll realize as soon as you get there that you only confused yourself trying to imagine it before. so basically get on stage as soon as possible, and as often as possible, so you can begin becoming yourself again while you're on stage. it's that simple

141957.ques: the US state i live in has exactly 2 area codes, and they both play the exact same tones when you dial them from a touch-tone phone. and i think that's pretty fuckin cool.
141957.answ: it's only half true, but still cool. all the tones on a touch tone phone are different, they have to be, otherwise the phone system wouldnt be able to tell the numbers apart. but what you probably are hearing is just one of the two tones in each number. each number has 2 tones together, and if i remember correctly all the numbers in a column have one of the tones the same, and all the numbers in a row have the other tone the same. so if you have 2 area codes that sound the same to you, that means they either hit the exact exact same rows or the exact same columns. looking at this map, i think the only state i see where this works is west virginia, which has only two area codes and they both go 'last column, middle column, first column'. so you will hear the same melody in both codes, while also hearing a different melody underneath that. as if you have 2 singers, one singer is singing the same melody twice, but the backup singer does it different the second time. to isolate the difference, and i will assume for a moment that this is west virginia (304/681) type 36363636 to hear the difference between those two. then type 80808080 to hear the difference between those two, and then type 41414141 to hear the difference between those two. with these toggles you will hear one of the tones changing while the other stays the same. then you will probably be start to hear the difference better between the two area codes

141971.ques: how does anyone ever get a very specific noise? im talking like sound effects. foley artists are a mystery to me.
141971.answ: really the trick with foley is, you'd be surprised what you can get away with. if you put something at the right time, you can almost make anything out of anything. Hopefully you will find yourself on a mega time- or budget-constraint sometime, because that's when you will actually realize "oh crap, i absolutely didnt need to find a [some specific object] i literally just did it with my shirt." What you wanna do is get the headphones on, and, actually, if you just do things with your hands directly in front of the mic, you can almost get all the sounds you ever need. Furthermore, i would argue that you SHOULD deliberately cut creative corners like this, because as of now, if you actually seek out the most 'realistic' thing, your reward will only be that the audience will just assume you could have used ai for it. or stock, or whatever. so you get hella bonus points for humble charm, starting now. but, as i said, you'd be shocked at how effective you can be with things that are totally not actually the thing. if you get the timing and length right, the imagination will do the rest and it will be arguably much stronger than if you had gone out of your way to find an actual [actual thing in the scene]

141972.ques: how do you sync your animations to your music (changing onscreen text with the lyrics, etc) so well? it's something i've always struggled with in my own editing but i'm sure it's bc of my method or my software
141972.answ: ultimately you'll need to have time navigation controls you're comfortable with (frame by frame, then something a little larger, then something a little larger) and then, crucially, you'll need to turn on audio-scrubbing mode. which means it plays you a tiny fraction of the audio at whatever frame you're at. so you can hear where you are. usually it takes some fooling around in the preferences and settings to get your techniques down, but you need frame by frame navigation and you need to hear the scrub. this is a normal feature for any software. possibly also may help to have drumming experience, because that just gives you a keen understanding of time in general

142008.ques: hello. im in a pickle. i have devoted my life to thus far to creating artwork, songs specifically, and for some reason couldnt commit to posting or releasing it. i have only released a small highly polished selection, maybe 1% of all the art ive made. and it's been so long now with ai it makes me feel like i missed a chance to put it out into the world when it should have been. the level of polish i seek deters me from from posting it now, but there is far too much music for all of it to have a music video at least without settling for something less than what i feel the music deserves. how do i apologize to my younger self/forgive my current self for robbing myself of the opportunity to share the art i made at the time when it was fresh and relevant? this infuriates me. my oldest songs feel like historical artifacts and it's painful to consider releasing at the moment and yet even more painful to continue holding them hostage and unheard.
142008.answ: eventually you have to deal with the fact that there are infinite possibilities and you will never be able to do them all. it's just a learning experience. But at some point you will hopefully discover that it IS possible to pick up one of those old pieces, and tweak it just a bit, particularly with very honest adherence to your ACTUAL FEELINGS about it, pack all the nostalgia you feel into it, and tweak it according to this in such a way that it will totally work. i think once you are able to do that for the first time, you will realize you have a whole world at your fingertips. what i've noticed is, it's always a good idea to envoke complete and total emotional honesty about what the song was, what it meant to you, and even sometimes include little additional details about how the song came about, IN the song as part of the rewrite. adding real life details about it that you may not have even thought to add back then. it's an amazing trick and when you can pull it off you'll feel like jumping directly onto the ceiling. very cool

142016.ques: i LOVE the part on off the map where the lyrics go "on the map and it feels.... just.... like there's somebody there ....here...." and so on. that part is just so beautiful and i dont even know what wizardry you pulled to make that happen. the thing is, this seems to be a very common pattern in all your songs, where there will be a specific part of the song that is extremely emotionally resonant. do you construct your songs intentionally to set up that one moment? do you consider a song's writing unfinished until you have a section that is mindblowingly beautiful? or do you consider all parts really beautiful, and maybe i just happen to personally find one section per song really beautiful?
142016.answ: mindblowing is absolutely the low bar that must be achieved with anything i do, otherwise it's just not worth it. (which part works on which people, if any, will always differ enormously, that is to be expected). that's why i'm here, at least. but this is not exactly something you can force to happen. you just have to accept the eb and flow. everything i've ever produced has these ups and downs to it, certain spots where the magic happens, and the other spots somewhat in between. this eb and flow is not something i would have tried to do on purpose, but i think it's something we all have to accept as one of the dynamics of life. you wouldnt believe how many improv sessions i have that are SO bad for a period of time, then the next section comes and it encapsulates all the cathartic recognition of how we felt about that, and feels so good, and you might think "cant you just cut out the bad part before" but the good part unfortunately makes no sense without the previous part because part of why the good part is so good is because it is reflecting directly about the pain we felt having gone through the bad part

142121.answ: put it this way, it would be very possible for one piece of audio to be described by one person as your first description ("random noises") and for the same piece of audio to be described by another person as your second description ("real music"). i think what you've done here deliberately is to set up your two descriptions in such a way that it would be unlikely for the same person to describe the same piece of audio both ways. 142192.ques: 7.12.26 1:25 am To ask a more ... pertinent(?) question, you know how often in jazz when you play a major 7 chord you often omit the 1 and 5 in favour for the bass note covering it? So Cmaj7 would be something like the bass player holding a C while the keyboard takes the E and B. Does this omitting-5 thing typically happen in triads too?
142192.answ: Cmaj7 will very often leave the C to only the bass player. also may often take away the 5. although in consideration for people listening to things outloud on their phone, this might make you wanna add the notes back in for fear that it would sound to them like E minor if they cant hear the bass. also in general, triads are more likely to need all 3 notes in the mid range (plus bass if there is bass) to be at their strongest, although there is a certain register where for example C G E (in that order lowest to high) works well. heck, an entire generation of EDM music was based on playing all the chords with no 5 anywhere, and just the root in the bass and 1 harmony note a tenth above, but dont take my word for it! try for yourself, see how these things sound, then notice if other people on their songs do it the same way you like to do it.

142220.answ: this might help: start browsing through other music to listen to. things from other artists, other times, other places. make a collection of things you like. then, with some of the ones you like, grab your instrument or paper or something and work out what they are doing with the chords. over time this will amount to some good broadening exposure for your songwriting repertoire. admittedly, this 4-chord-loop phenomenon became huge in the computer era (especially post 2000 or so) because it became an easy way to work, to have something that repeats. but before then, especially if you go back pre-1980, it didnt even occur to anyone to use 4bar loops because you'd just have to play it again every time anyway. so that's why you get so many 'different' things that happen. verses that go 'different' in the second half, choruses being different, half-bars being thrown in, etc. start browsing through things and start making a collection of the things there that you like the most. should be a lot of fun. This 4loop thing is something that the wider world has been addicted to for a while now, not just you. which is precisely what makes it so enticing now to venture more freely into slightly more creative waters, roadmapwise

142250.ques: crazy ai thing - i work in a nursing home and i have to schedule appointments for the residents here, and i was having a huuuuge problem with emails that i send to have radiology scheduled. in my professional life, I tend to use precise, textbook phrasing, punctuation, spelling, and capitalization. I found that the emails I wrote in this style were not reaching the schedulers for the hospital radiology department, and I never got a response. however, when i throw in at least one "typo," i always get a response back in an hour or so. so my conclusion is that they have some kind of filter for AI-generated emails, and my professionalism was being punished. how Fucked would i be if i went back to college??
142250.answ: interesting to hear this. it's been a few years now that i've begun to speculate that genuine human-ness should be rapidly becoming a sought after trait, including and especially in professional contexts. however, it's worth giving college the benefit of the doubt here: they're not going to not have noticed this (sorry for double negative). if what you've noticed is true, then no college in its right mind would continue advocating that you talk like a proper robot. in fact, in a way i'd like to think that they always encouraged genuineness, even on a professional level. but who knows..... Anyway, this excites me generally. it's always refreshing to see insincerity (such as "Sincerely,") not winning any extra points. because there always seems to be this lingering sort of negative viewpoint saying that insincerity DOES win points, and i'm always like 'you wait and see, in the end it doesnt'. so it's always reassuring for me to see signs that creativity is at least intended to be valued over generic predictability which of course ai has got a lock on

142281.ques: at the bottom of your jazz page, it says that each song is performed by your "fake jazz ensemble" if it's fake then why do i hear music?
142281.answ: the word 'fake' here evokes a couple of different things. starting around the 1950s there was something called "fakebooks" which had very basic sheet music for popular standards (usually just melody and chords, not the full arrangement, maybe sometimes not even exactly accurate). and people used to jam on those. This is essentially the exact same game i'm playing here (in many cases i am taking these song choices straight from the 'Real Book' which is possibly the most well-known fakebook of my lifetime, in other cases i'm just doing them from memory). And the other reason why it is a fake ensemble is because it's actually just me. Another resason you might call it fake is because in a 'jazz ensemble' you might expect to have an acoustic horn instrument (such as saxophone or trumpet) playing the lead, and in this case i'm using an obnoxious synth instead. so that's 3 different reasons to invoke the word 'fake'

142282.ques: why do so many people insist on using choruses? i feel like verses do just fine on their own
142282.answ: i think more people think there are more choruses than there actually are choruses. i think you might be fond of a very standard style which used to be used constantly and is STILL used quite a lot (i use it all the time), known as "AABA". you might say it goes 'verse, verse, B section, verse'. and the verse usually has the title in it. So is the verse actually the chorus? maybe, even though it has different lyrics every time and it starts the song. so then is the B section the chorus? not really, if anything it sounds more like a bridge. it's AABA. then usually after the AABA you'll have an instrumental solo over maybe one A, then the lyrics jump back in for a second B, then to one more A with a tag at the end where you repeat the last line or something like that. Additionally, besides AABA, there are also many other kinds of song forms which are very popular and which dont really have a 'chorus'. as i said, it's more often that people 'think' all songs have choruses than they actually do

142364.ques: When did they start using click tracks? Was there a pretty rapid explosion of bands using them or was it a slow progression of it becoming more and more common? I could imagine that there would've been some early push-back (as there always is with new technology) that playing to a click would take away from the musician's personal feel
142364.answ: click sort of came along with technology in general. first you had drum machines, so anyone playing with a drum machine is getting a click. but then aside from that you have just recording into computers in general. as long as youre going into protools or whatever, you might as well let protools know what bar youre on, and if you do that then you have to play to a click. the click is sort of something that snuck in through the side door. sure, i'm sure they would have had technology to record things to a mechanical metronome back in the day, but there was never a reason to do it. the click is just sort of a side effect of the times. so from the 80s onward, anyone using midi or drum machines is almost definitely on a click, and then from about 2000 onward you start to hear everyone on click, even guitar bands etc.

142452.ques: by improvising vocally I am able to create pretty good songs sometimes. they're not as good as the ones that pop in my head out of nowhere but they're close enough. however even though they're musically cool, the lyrics are a garbled nonsense most of the time and so I have to replace them afterwards when I make the actual song so that it actually means something. this is a tedious task and the lines I'm left with almost always sound and rhyme worse than the originals. do you ever need to do this or did you train yourself to spit bars first try
142452.answ: the chords melody and words are, ideally, all written together. so that means, if the song was 'improvised', it would have to be done while playing and singing at the same time. this can happen, and actually if you think about it, all writing, no matter what, is a form of improvisation at some point because when you originally come up with the idea, there it is you just made it up. and when things come to you, they seem to come at full speed or not at all. lyric replacements can be a curse and they often arent as good as the first version. if you have to replace the lyrics, then i would argue what happened was "the music got ahead of the words" because you now think you have the right melody but no words. this causes problems when either the music or words get too far ahead. best results are when it all is born together

142538.ques: why do you think 'classical' music (say european music from the 18th and 19th century) so rarely employs simple chord progressions? say C-E-F-Fm, or C-Em-Am-F, Cm-Ab-Eb-Bb, whatever. they are all amazingly effective, as in they can sound amazing when used well. and, of course, you are never obliged to keep a 4-loop for an entire song -- i mean that too can be cool, but then you can always introduce some variety, whatever you want and yet these simple chord progressions seem to feature so rarely in classical music. it's perplexing to me. composers can't have been oblivious to the potential of these harmonies, right? not when they are so comparatively simple and therefore easy to discover. did composers feel that these harmonies simply didn't sound good? (in which case they would be at odds with quite a few modern audiences) or did they feel that they had to show off somehow, and so they couldn't afford to use simple harmony?
142538.answ: you say this kind of music "so rarely employs simple chord progressions" i disagree fully. i think what's happening is they dont put chord symbols on the page because, in the case of the kind of music you mentioned, most of the music is played 1-person-per-note. so the chords arent written on the page. but they're still there. and they're still just as 'simple' as the examples you had in mind. Then the next thing you mention is loops, which is a separate issue mostly coming from computers. in music it's always good to have sameness and differentness. sameness and differentness. at a certain point computers made it extremely easy to loop the same chords over and over again, so, to the extent you can get away with it and still make interesting music, it's used. but if there were no such technology, .... you'd repeat some things sometimes but then take the opportunity for differentness also. Also in the world of looped chords, if youre strong enough and if you can keep your head straight, you can break the loop, and people can and do, to very strong effect. And another issue that factors into this conversation is you are selecting a certain kind of music which is the most expensive. already having said that most of the popular 'classical' things have chords that are just as 'simple' as anything that was ever popular, on top of that, if we're talking about popular songs with words, things that people sing at parties, then those things are going to definitely have simple chords, and will often be sung with no chords at all if no one happens to have an instrument on hand. and if they do, .... they're just gonna be a couple of chords. Not a forever-loop per se, because, like i was saying, there's no reason to necessarily be locked into that. but, repetition, yes. and changes when needed. I think what might actually be very enlightening for you at this juncture is to listen through the popular music charts through the years all the way from 2026 back to 1898 (or as far back as you can go). i think a number of realizations will probably jump out at you. i think you will slowly start to find that there is no categorical 'change' in what is or is not effective, but to whatever extent you ever notice some important technique or trick is lacking at any point in time, i can promise it will always work, and these represent ripe opportunities for someone to come along and employ it afresh

And here's what does not work: you trying to make something you don't like, based on the 'logic' that someone who doesn't like what you like will like what you don't like. that DOES NOT work. Imagine you are someone who can't tell the difference between blue and green, you only can see "yellow or not yellow", but you know that some people like blue and green pictures which you can't really even understand, but you wanna try doing it even though you cant see what youre doing, so you take a bunch of "not yellow" and mash it all together, it looks just as bad to you as those other blue-green pictures, but it also looks like shit to the blue-green seeers because you couldnt see what youre doing so you actually couldnt even make a picture of anything. in blue-green world, you are not detecting what is 'good/bad' about it. you are painting with colors you cant see. you must make things which you can detect. it's the only detector you actually have. and, as a creative expressor, your purpose in life, perhaps, is to express things in terms of how you currently see it

142677.ques: I've been working on a song for a few months and as I steadily worked my way through all the production steps, I became more and more discouraged, thinking that it was getting further and further from the "magic" of the original sketch. But then I went back and listened to the original sketch, and it was objectively way worse than my current prototype. So I realized that I must be growing numb to my own creations, and I don't know how to judge whether a particular musical decision/direction is a good one anymore, which is scary. I've heard you make the analogy that "making things you think other people will like is like painting with colors you can't see", and it's great advice, but now the colors I CAN see (or used to see so vividly) are starting to fade. I have faith that they'll return eventually, but does this ever happen to you, and do you have any navigational advice when the terrain all turns grey?
142677.answ: yes, i have a different set of analogies for this. i've heard filmmakers talk about this, and what gets especially bad is when your movie has a lot of 'funny' in it. a lot of stuff deliberately meant to be funny and make you laugh. People making full length movies based on funny will be the first to tell you, you have to have a lot of faith that you once thought this was funny. because after hearing it so many times during production it will lose its funnyness. This happens to funnyness perhaps the fastest, but it happens to some degree with all forms of creativity. And the other analogy i can offer you, also from filmmaking, it has been said that making a movie is like making a 100 foot mural from 3 inches away. you can spend a lifetime trying to find different ways around this aspect to building creative things

142971.ques: I feel like I wake up every day with a different brain. I will spend an entire day obsessed with metallurgy, memorizing the tensile strengths of different metals, and the next day I'm ready to sell everything I own to pursue a life as a close-up street magician. I have (barely) managed to compress the scope enough that I don't ruin/uproot my life every week, but I don't know what to do with all these extra minds. They're really interesting, and most of them are intelligent, and I would give them away if I could. The most productive thing I've found is to fill up worlds with them, but the dilemma is that they tend to dissipate before I'm finished rendering. What is my question. How does one practically tolerate/live with an infinitely electic mind? How does one financially sustain themselves?
142971.answ: this is a lifelong project, figuring this out, but it's pretty good news. you have a superpower. it will take some cleverness to get it rigged up to properly take advantage of it so it doesnt trip over itself, but the fact that you have this problem to solve makes it even more rewarding when you start to figure it out. So then you get not only the reward of solving this challenge, but then on top of that you'll have the unimpeded superpowers to make use of. which reminds me, one of the most common mistakes is to impede those superpowers, just because you dont at first know how to make sense of them. they're there, it's just you've got a nice hefty puzzle to solve before they can work properly

143211.ques: idk what to do when i have a pencil in my hand and eyes on paper but i know i want to do something. What would your first steps be?
143211.answ: this is kind of a hellish blank stare, which you kind of dont really need. But, admittedly, sometimes it's inescapable as your weird destiny, because you want so desperately the joys and benefits of writing, you get very attached to this 'page' which is seemingly the gateway toward bringing you there. But, of course, staring directly at it when you have nothing else other than staring at the page itself, is a cursed voidsituation. However, we can address this quite appropriately with reverse psychology. If you are staring blankly at the page, ....... basically destroy the page. sabotage. it's a lot of fun, and sets you up nicely to do another page. sometimes the deal with this kind of trick is, plan on doing a whole pile of crap-pages. Have you ever heard the sound of someone starting up a lawn mower? that's about like what you wanna do, with garbagewriting on the first few rounds. gives you something to react to, actually

143241.ques: I've been noticing... that I want to make the Best songs and the Best albums ever ... and like so far it sounds like "yeah seems pretty normal"... But! I feel like I only want to do it to feel proud of myself and make people finally realize what i can do and make them take me more seriously and see me as a Real Artist and also so people will actually listen to my music and look at all my earlier work in retrospect afteri release this Big awesome album that i want to make... and i'm thinking... am i really doing this all for the love of the art and the creative process or am i just doing because i want the same praise as i see given to all the artists everyone around me loves... i'm always so jealous of the praise they get and i want some of that too. I want to be known. i want people to look up to me. i feel like i Have to do this big thing so i can actually be proud of myself and live with myself and what i've done and realize my full potential... but is this really the way? i'm sure great art could come out from this. great art HAS come from this kind of mentality. but i feel like it's getting way too competitive... the pressure doesn't feel right anymore. it doesn't feel like i'm doing it just for the love of the art and to make something good.. i'm not sure if i'm enjoying the creative process as much anymore with this kind of mentality. i feel like i have to make something so ambitious and great. what do you think?
143241.answ: it's perfectly fine that you have these kinds of things as a motivator. as earthly human animals, we all surely have these kinds of motivations in the mix. But the hilarious part, which you eventually will realize, sometimes by accident, is actually really 'good music' is actually impossible to contrive or predict, and the only time the real good stuff ever comes along is when, somehow, maybe by accident, someone ends up doing or saying something they really feel. So whether or not you openly admit that youre going for the genuine, you'll find out regardless that your songwriting mechanism will inexplicably refuse to cough up the goods until you are in a genuine state of feeling. And again, one way or another, this usually reveals itself by mistake. Over and over again, you'll facepalm at how hilarious it is when you realize, for the millionth time again, why it's called 'playing'

143252.ques: What new animation techniques were you deliberately trying to try out in 'off the map'? i feel as though youre always trying something new so im curious
143252.answ: the sentiment that marks 'off the map', surely, is rebellion against ai. Not even rebelling against actual ai, it's more just the perceived encroachment of ai, for the audience. We all watch things now with a dreary skeptical eye, constantly debating with ourselves "is this ai? is that ai? ... and if its not, then it's a shame this person spent so much time on it thanklessly because we're not even sure we believe it's real even if it is", so, this being the first video that i made truly within the era of this kind of haze, that mindset was front and center. you'll find me eager to prove i'm human on this one. a commonly used technique on this one is being super careless with leaving trash behind in the 3D space. previous lyric lines can often be spotted in the distance, at screwy angles, just because they were left there. Around the time that this was made, it was generally believed that ai tends to be bad at object permanence. so i am taking extra special delights here in leaving my garbage around. and of course one of the most important 'new animation techniques' to be most urgently tried and perfected is being simple as fuck, because i have 100s of these songs to do and i need to be able to actually get to them cause otherwise seriously whats the point

143256.ques: the way i deal with key changes is by making, like, the chord right before changing the key to be some real dissonant one like maybe some diminished chord and then putting a less dissonant one like your typical major or major 7th in the next key. like, say im on E major, and i wanns change to idk G# major: first is chord E, then dissonant off-key D# diminished (idk i randomize this one usually) and then to change chord i go with G# major. why? because this dissonant chord here is sorta unpleasant, or at least unpleasant in comparison to the following chord which is G major. so like, the change feels "good" because i like, build some tension, and then release it, to sort of make this "refreshing" feeling. does this make any sense?
143256.answ: in a few more years, if you keep playing, you wont have time to explain it this way, you'll be so caught up in the feelings. And, the words (or scene). Sort of like when you carry a cake across an obstacle course ...... you are not using any conscious analytical method to determine where you step. you just know where you wanna step, and you gotta get that cake somewhere. Even crazier when you are supposed to make up your own destination for the cake. youre going to need to find out the reason for the cake. And to think, just a few years ago you were so focused on your feet alone
